score.note: Raw halfwords are phase-dominated: the entry region differs only by a register-allocation shuffle (r1/r2/r5 permutation, one mov sl placement), long runs align between clusters, and the large +/- runs are literal-pool words placed at different sites. The 20-byte length gap is pool-word count, not missing logic. The evidenced GS2 inline-register-call route improves differing_halfwords 3914 -> 3912 and wrong_instructions 2574 -> 2570.

shape.architecture: Twelve-ROM master: games/gs1/recon/ja/main/080b2b0c.c is the shared body, written against ~60 BATTLE_* hook macros (362 uses). GS1 editions bind the hooks to GS1 semantics; games/gs2/recon/ja/main/battle_delta.h rebinds them with the sequel's grown logic (extra effect/heal/KO/guard cases) plus per-edition literal headers and ~200 per-edition callee retargets. BATTLE_SECOND_ACTOR reshapes struct BattlePlan in games/gs1/include/battle_types.h.
shape.constraint: The master body must stay byte-exact for gs1-en: measured 6332/6332 at 0 differing halfwords when wrapped as Func_080bbb0c against roms/gs1-en.gba. Every GS2-side repair must live in the hook bodies, the delta headers, or GS2-only conditionals -- never in unguarded shared text.
shape.gs1_status: main:080bbb0c is production-exact and relink-proven byte-exact in all six GS1 editions (exact-main-builds, location_methods asaaaa). Six of the twelve ROMs stand.
shape.gs2_editions: All six GS2 editions are core-identical for this owner (games/gs2/recon/cross-edition.json): one exact edition source closes all six through the existing literal/retarget headers.

notes: Accepted compiler route: `-mthumb-inline-register-call` restores GCC's historical `mov lr, rN; .hword 0xf800` Thumb indirect-call lowering. The GS2 EN ROM contains 1,828 instances of that signature while GS1 EN contains none, so the route is GS2-only and default-off in agscc. At this owner's single site it reproduces the four reference bytes exactly.

The JA-native GS1 candidate (games/gs1/recon/ja/main/080b2b0c.c wrapped as Func_080b2b0c) measures 6332/6332 at 272 differing halfwords against roms/gs1-ja.gba; since the production EN object relinks byte-exact at the JA address, those 272 halfwords are JA-side binding/literal gaps in the wrapper, not core differences.
Recovered only from retained/located owner bytes in the approved local ROMs, the adopted GS1 EN source, in-repository headers, and the approved compiler.
This candidate claims zero DONE bytes.

rejected_experiments.result: The compiler segfaults while compiling this owner. This is a recorded miss, not evidence for the reference's literal-pool route; the pool option is not adopted for this translation unit.
Neutral on the call model: GCC still emits `_call_via_r3`; 8272/8300 bytes, 3914 differing halfwords, 2570 wrong instructions. This is not the missing route.

GCC changes the call to `_interwork_call_via_r3`, confirming the site is controlled by the Thumb indirect-call backend, but that is not the ROM's inline register-call sequence and the verifier correctly has no canonical address for the absent veneer. Not adopted.

rejected_experiments.experiment: declare 0x03000730 as a direct absolute function instead of a function pointer
rejected_experiments.result: Regressed to 8252/8300 bytes, 3961 differing halfwords, and 2597 wrong instructions; GCC emits a direct branch rather than the ROM's register call. Reverted.

rejected_experiments.experiment: BATTLE_HEAL_PREP with all arms sharing one Math_Div through a goto tail (num/den computed per arm)
rejected_experiments.result: Over-merges: the candidate falls to 8272 bytes as the sign-extend epilogue is shared too; the reference shares the divide call site but keeps per-arm preparation. 3917 halfwords, 2618 wrong instructions. Reverted.

rejected_experiments.experiment: else arm spelled with direct both-width loads (maxu then maxv via casts of &target->max_hp)
rejected_experiments.result: GCC folds the second load into a sign-extend of the first; the reference emits two loads (ldrh then ldrsh). The GS1 pointer-walk idiom defeats the fold and is kept for that arm only.

expressed: BATTLE_HEAL_PREP direct-access respell: the 0x4c/0x47/0x46 arms now read max_hp through direct casts, emitting the reference's movs #52 / ldrsh reg-offset + ldrh immediate forms instead of pre-adding 52 into the base; the else arm keeps the GS1 pointer walk to preserve its unfolded double-width load. Cluster verified locally against the reference; wrong_instructions 2608 -> 2574.

Remaining in this cluster: the reference shares one Math_Div call site across the calling arms (arms branch to a common 0x1458 tail with the divisor staged per arm) while the candidate duplicates the call; the exact sharing boundary excludes the maxu sign-extend, so a plain goto over-merges.
